findings_for_tadashi.A_quiet_note_403: LEAD-notify quiet thread-note leg uses alertDiscordOps (unified-alert Hub/repair-chain bot = test-1), which is NOT a member of the dept Lead's channel in multi-Lead topology → 403. Episode still progresses via DB + founder page still posts via owner bot. plugin.ts:6339 suspiciousThreadPoster→alertDiscordOps.postToThread
findings_for_tadashi.B_addThreadMember_403: Founder added to issue thread via addThreadMember also uses the Hub bot (test-1) → 403 Missing Access. So the founder is NOT added as a thread member in this env.
findings_for_tadashi.C_no_at_mention_BY_DESIGN: Founder page posts 🚨 with allowed_mentions:{users:[owner]} but content never contains <@ownerId> (postFounderThreadCore only sets allowed_mentions, a filter; createFounderPager content has no <@>). PR-C test (detection-escalation-sinks.test.ts:107) asserts only mentionUserId is passed, NOT <@ in content. So founder page does NOT @-ping; it relies on thread membership. Plan E2 'mentions[].id' assertion was over-specified.
findings_for_tadashi.combined_risk: In multi-project prod where the alert Hub bot lacks membership in a dept Lead channel: founder page POSTS (owner bot) but founder is neither @-pinged (by design) NOR added to the thread (Hub-bot 403) → founder may not be notified unless already watching the channel. Needs Tadashi judgment on prod Hub-bot channel access.
findings_for_tadashi.env_limits: (1) test runners spawn on Fable-5 (quota exhausted) → idle at startup; gap injected via real flywheel-comm ask CLI targeting the SLOT commdb with the runner's real execId (env-accident, not a shortcut; DB row byte-identical to runner-originated). (2) test bots lack MANAGE_ROLES → cannot grant Hub bot dept-channel access to remove the confound.
